**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Execute the memory CLI only from a trusted checkout**

When this script is invoked from a PR or detached review worktree, `root` comes from the caller's current checkout and this line runs that checkout's `.claude/hooks/contextdb_cli.py`, allowing a PR that modifies the file to execute arbitrary code on the orchestrator host. `uv run --help` describes `uv run` as running a command or script and says `--no-project` only avoids project/workspace discovery, so that flag does not establish trust. Resolve the CLI from the trusted script/main checkout or verify the checkout before execution; the environment residual in the threat table does not mitigate this PR-controlled-code path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/61290da8801cd714788814a6a6d077a37773a044/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Close the threat row for all three scripts**

This `closed` disposition covers `dispatch.sh`, `three-repeat.sh`, and `bus-read.sh`, but its sole selector only verifies that one mismatched hash prevents dispatch. It cannot close the stated risks in the class search or bus-history parser, including the untrusted CLI execution path above. Split the row per script or reference tests that actually close every risk covered by this broad control.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/61290da8801cd714788814a6a6d077a37773a044/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject files with multiple trailing newlines**

When the line file contains a valid message followed by one or more blank lines, Bash command substitution strips all trailing newline characters before the check on line 34, so this accepts a multi-line file and dispatches only its first nonblank line despite the stated exactly-one-line contract. Preserve a sentinel while reading or otherwise validate the file's physical line count before stripping the single permitted terminator.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record the dispatched line in the acceptance record**

Once the pending playbook-rules change is enabled, every TASK, ACCEPTANCE, and PING sent through this script is expected to be recorded under the current acceptance record's `dispatch:` key with its bus/read evidence (`.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T128-playbook-rules-a04.md`, item 1), but the script accepts no record path and this final action only invokes `agmsg-dispatch`. Consequently every successful dispatch omits the evidence that the new procedure relies on to report a seat as working, even though this task says landing these scripts makes that rule true.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the TASK hash before dispatching**

When an `AGMSG-TASK` omits `task_sha256=`, this loop has no matching token, reaches the final `exec`, and sends a task whose file was never authenticated. This defeats the repository invariant that every task dispatch is hash-bound and can let a worker act on mutable task contents before the later merge gate detects the omission; require `task_file=` and a valid `task_sha256=` for TASK messages before checking any optional hashes. The threat table's closed test exercises only a present-but-wrong hash, so it does not close this omission path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/5b6d5f24d2b056803eea4dd4275ffcd79c2bb16c/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject conflicting hash source fields**

When a line contains both sibling forms, this precedence can validate the wrong artifact: for example, `design=design.md design_file=other.md design_sha256=<hash-of-other.md>` passes because `design_file` wins, while the dispatched protocol line still identifies `design.md` as the design. This defeats the intended hash binding and is not covered by the threat table's mismatch test; reject ambiguous sibling pairs or enforce the protocol's explicit mappings such as `design_sha256` to `design=`.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/374fc1711e50c7166f68571ebba41d6d617c1807/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid self-naming as the dispatch recipient**

Whenever an acceptance record is supplied, this agent-qualified `history.sh` call runs in the orchestrator's session with `$to` as its agent identity. The repository documents that `history.sh <team> <agent>` self-names the caller's pane and session (`.orchestration/reports/dotfiles-T65-agent-stop-gate-a01.md:30`), so recording a dispatch to a worker silently relabels the orchestrator as that worker; the stubbed history test cannot expose this host effect. Read the marker through a non-mutating team-wide/storage-facade path instead.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/374fc1711e50c7166f68571ebba41d6d617c1807/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not record a stale match after dispatch failure**

If `agmsg-dispatch` exits before inserting a message—for example, its pane lookup or `send.sh` can fail—the script still searches history and appends a record. When an identical TASK or PING was sent previously, the old row satisfies the body/from/to match, so the acceptance record falsely claims another dispatch even though this invocation exits 1. Record only a bus row proven to have been created by this invocation, distinguishing pre-send failures from the sent-but-unread case.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/374fc1711e50c7166f68571ebba41d6d617c1807/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject duplicate file tokens before hashing**

Fresh evidence beyond the sibling-field fix: `value_of` still returns only the first occurrence of a repeated key, so `task_file=safe.md task_file=other.md task_sha256=<hash-of-safe.md>` passes validation and is dispatched with an unauthenticated second task path. A recipient interpreting the later token can therefore act on content that the hash never covered; reject duplicate source-field tokens before selecting the file. The closed mismatch test does not exercise this ambiguity.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/e707c7642a9ec523898a45531d88096af265cc3f/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add a threat row for acceptance-record mutation**

Fresh functionality added by amendment 1 makes `dispatch.sh` parse a caller-selected acceptance record, inspect untrusted bus output, and rewrite that record after sending, but the dispatch rows here cover only hash verification and malformed message lines. Consequently the new record path/content and post-send evidence-association boundary has no threat-table row or mapped control, despite this repository requiring every trust-boundary change to be assessed for missing rows; add a dedicated row covering that input and mutation path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/e707c7642a9ec523898a45531d88096af265cc3f/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Terminate option parsing before passing the class**

For an allowed leading-hyphen slug such as `--help`, this invocation does not search for the class: the local `contextdb memory search --help` usage lists `[-h] [--session SESSION] [--limit LIMIT] query [query ...]`, so `--help` prints help and exits successfully, while `--limit` is consumed as an option and fails for lack of a value. Because the validator accepts both values under `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, an S1 class can therefore skip or break the required CompactionDB search; pass an option terminator before the class or reject option-shaped slugs. The threat row's test covers spaces and semicolons but not this accepted CLI-option input.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/58ecd7538f160a317258aaa9e74eab01a308c286/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the acceptance record belongs to the requested task**

When `<task>.md` is stale or copied from another task but still contains a `ledger` array, this condition accepts it without checking the block's required `task` identity. Its unrelated classes then replace the GitHub fallback and can either trigger a false S1 reset or suppress the requested task's real repeated class before the later gate runs. Require the record's `task` field to equal `${task}` before treating its ledger as authoritative; the counter threat row's residual review/test inspection does not mitigate an identity mismatch in this input.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/58ecd7538f160a317258aaa9e74eab01a308c286/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize digits in hash-field names**

When an accepted message carries a hash field whose name contains a digit, such as `artifact2_sha256=` or the repository's existing `a02_expected_sha256=` naming form, this regex does not recognize it, so the loop silently dispatches the line without checking the named file or digest. This violates the script's central promise to recompute every `*_sha256=` token and lets a PING or ACCEPTANCE authenticate an artifact only syntactically; include digits in the field-name grammar or reject every unrecognized token ending in `_sha256`. The closed mismatch test exercises only `task_sha256`, so it does not close this path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L77-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/58ecd7538f160a317258aaa9e74eab01a308c286/AGENTS.md#L77-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the record task before appending dispatch evidence**

When the operator accidentally supplies another task's acceptance record—for example, the line has `task_id=t` while the parsed block has `"task":"u"`—the script appends the dispatch without comparing those identities, permanently placing task `t`'s evidence under task `u`. Validate the line's task ID against the existing record's task (and preferably its filename) before sending. Fresh evidence after the acceptance-record threat row was added: its named test exercises only a matching `task=t` record and therefore does not close this association error.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/4fc6040f0c029d2f39568f2a3ccc129ca97537c6/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Write the acceptance record atomically**

Because this overwrite occurs after the bus message has been sent, an interruption, disk-full error, or short write during `write_text` can leave the acceptance record truncated or partially written while the dispatch has already succeeded. That destroys the existing gate evidence and leaves no reliable record of the sent line; write a temporary file in the same directory and atomically replace the record only after the complete content is durable. The closed threat-table test exercises only a successful write and cannot detect this failure mode.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/4fc6040f0c029d2f39568f2a3ccc129ca97537c6/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a task ID on every dispatched message**

When an otherwise accepted TASK, ACCEPTANCE, or PING omits `task_id=`, this prefix check succeeds and the line reaches `agmsg-dispatch`; when a record is supplied, the later `task is not None` condition also skips the association check, so the malformed orphan message can be sent and recorded. The protocol requires `task_id=<id>` for all three message types (`home/dot_agents/skills/agmsg-orchestration/SKILL.md:100,126,136`), so reject a missing, empty, or duplicated task ID before processing hashes or records; the threat table has no row or test for this malformed-identity path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/c8fb09b00bc3e79fdce2f23617c3e6aadaa55e5e/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate ledger rows before trusting the record**

When a matching acceptance record has a `ledger` array whose entries are not the required `{id, class}` objects—for example `[{}, {}, {}]` during partial or malformed record generation—this condition still treats the record as authoritative. The later grouping converts all three missing classes to `null` and emits a false `S1: class=invalid count=3`; with fewer malformed rows, `$rec != null` instead suppresses the GitHub-title fallback and can hide a real three-repeat. Validate every ledger row before accepting the record, otherwise treat the block as invalid/null; the threat-table residual's review/test inspection does not mitigate this runtime input path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/ba4d47620ebf60536198927c04c00205539b8568/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use consistent tokenization for record association**

When a valid separator is a tab, such as `AGMSG-PING v1 \ttask_id=t`, Bash tokenization accepts exactly one non-empty task ID, but `line.split(" ")` does not find it. The record identity check is therefore skipped, allowing the message to be sent and appended to a record whose `task` is different. Fresh evidence beyond the prior identity fix is that the validator and recorder now tokenize the same accepted line differently; parse `task_id` once or split on all shell whitespace. The closed acceptance-record test does not cover this path.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize acceptance-record updates**

When two successful dispatches target the same acceptance record concurrently, both append subprocesses can read the same pre-update JSON, add only their own entry, and then atomically replace the file; whichever replacement runs last silently discards the other dispatch evidence. Atomic rename prevents partial files but does not prevent this lost-update race, so protect the read-modify-write sequence with a per-record lock or a compare-and-retry step. The closed acceptance-record test exercises only one writer and therefore does not close concurrent mutation.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse a capped history before dispatching**

When the team already has at least 100,000 messages and the oldest row in the returned window is an identical prior dispatch, sending the new row displaces that old match, leaving the before/after match counts equal; line 182 then reports that no row was added and omits evidence even though the send succeeded. [agmsg documents `history.sh`](https://github.com/fujibee/agmsg/blob/main/docs/design.md) as selecting the newest entries and displaying them oldest-first, and `bus-read.sh` already treats reaching its limit as incomplete. Count the pre-read rows and refuse a capped view before sending, or identify the inserted row by a stable ID. The closed acceptance-record test uses an uncapped history and does not cover this association failure.
